title: Internal Categoricity and the Generic Multiverse: the consistency of a non-standard model of $MV$ all of whose worlds are uncountable and transitive (Proposition 10)
author: Toby Meadows
work: Internal Categoricity and the Generic Multiverse
difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the consistency, from the hypothesis that $L_{\omega_1}$ satisfies ZFC, of a non-standard model of the generic multiverse all of whose worlds are uncountable and transitive, and it is carried by the longest single argument of the paper: a 117-line forcing proof, longer than the 78-line proof of Theorem 13 and the 69-line proof of Theorem 29. The proof has to build the model rather than quote one. It introduces Silver's collapse forcing $\mathbb{S}_X$ with its first and second domains, explains how it differs from Levy's collapse $\mathbb{C}_{\omega_1}$ through the countable completeness of its second domain, handles the metamathematical point that such a generic need not exist by working virtually under $\Vdash_{\mathbb{S}_{\omega_1}}$ inside $L$, states and proves a two-part claim inside the proof (part (1) that every set in $[\omega_1]^{\omega_1}\cap V[H]$ has a countably infinite subset in $L$, by a descending sequence of conditions chosen with least second domain and a fusion-style bound, and part (2) that a $\mathbb{C}_{\omega_1}$-generic $G$ yields a set with no countably infinite subset in $L$), defines the name $\dot A$ from conditions acting on $0$, recalls the abstract weak-density transfer fact for order-preserving maps, embeds $\mathbb{C}_{\omega_1}$ weakly densely into $Add(\omega_1,1)$ through $\sigma(p)(\alpha)=1$ iff $p(0,\alpha)=1$, and closes with the finite-condition argument. None of this is examined at the level of an ordinary PhD qualifying examination, where forcing appears as the standard Cohen and Levy collapse together with the definability, chain-condition and truth lemmas; here the candidate must construct a new consistency model, control two different collapsing forcings at once and carry a fusion argument inside a claim embedded in the proof. With the paper's own section 2 retained as context, so that the axioms of $MV$ and the prerequisites are supplied, the unit still stands well above the bar: H3.
